item.title: Yamanaka Onsen: A Gorge-Side Hot Spring Town Praised by Basho — Guide
item.description: Yamanaka Onsen was praised by the famed 17th-century haiku poet Matsuo Basho for its restorative waters during his travels through the region, and the town retains a genuine literary and historical atmosphere alongside its traditional hot spring bathhouses. Beyond the baths, visitors can walk the scenic Kakusenkei Gorge trail along the Daishoji River, cross the striking red Korogi Bridge, and browse shops connected to Kutani porcelain, one of the Kaga region’s celebrated ceramic craft traditions.

item.title: Yamashiro Onsen: A 1,300-Year-Old Hot Spring Town — Guide
item.description: Yamashiro Onsen is one of the Kaga region’s oldest hot spring towns, its waters discovered some 1,300 years ago according to local tradition, and the town today centres on Kosoyu, a beautifully restored public bathhouse rebuilt in the style of the Meiji-era original, alongside the still-functioning Soyu bathhouse next door. The town also has strong ties to Kutani porcelain, one of Japan’s most celebrated ceramic traditions, with a small museum and shops nearby offering a look at the distinctive, richly coloured pottery style associated with the region.
